Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

satisfy verb

content someone, meet their wishes

also satisfied, be satisfied with, content with, satisfy someone, satisfaction, to your satisfaction, you can’t satisfy everyone, as one wished

classical

Cic. Att. 2.4.3: dē geōgraphiā dabō operam ut tibi satis faciam

satisfaciō, satisfacere, satisfēcī, satisfactum

verb, third conjugation (-iō), with the dative; also written as two words, satis faciō

satisfy, content (a person)

To do enough for someone, to meet what he wants or expects (Lewis & Short). It also means to make amends, to apologise (alicui satisfacere after an offence), and to pay a creditor in full; the context tells which.

Other words

  • contentus, contenta, contentum — satisfied, content (with)

    adjective: with the ablative of the thing, declension · also used · classical · Phaedr. 3.18.10–14: omnēsque propriīs sunt contentae dōtibus; Traupman 150

    “Satisfied with”: contentus suīs rēbus, content with what one has (Cic. Parad. 51, Lewis & Short). A different word from contentus, “strained”, the participle of contendō.

  • placeō, placēre, placuī, placitum — please, be approved

    verb, second conjugation, with the dative · also used · classical

    Latin often turns “I’m satisfied with it” round: mihi placet, it pleases me.

  • ex sententiā — to one’s satisfaction, as one wished

    ex with the ablative; with a possessive: ex tuā sententiā, to your satisfaction · also used · classical · Plaut. Ps. 2.4.72: auspiciō liquidō atque ex sententiā (Lewis & Short s.v. avis); Traupman 107: to your satisfaction, ex tuā sententiā

  • satisfactiō, satisfactiōnis f. — an apology, excuse; amends

    noun, third declension · avoid · classical · Caes. BG 6.9: Ubiōrum satisfactiōnem accēpit (Lewis & Short); Cic. Fam. 7.13.1 (Lewis & Short)

    A false friend: classically an apology or explanation offered to someone, and after Augustus amends for an injury (Tac. Germ. 21), not the feeling of being satisfied (Lewis & Short).

Examples

  • dē geōgraphiā dabō operam ut tibi satis faciam; sed nihil certī polliceor.

    About the geography, I’ll do my best to satisfy you; but I promise nothing definite.Cic. Att. 2.4.3

  • tibi fōrma, vīrēs aquilae, lusciniō melos, augurium corvō, laeva cornīcī ōmina, omnēsque propriīs sunt contentae dōtibus.

    to you beauty, to the eagle strength, to the nightingale song, to the raven augury, to the crow omens on the left, and all are content with their own gifts.Phaedr. 3.18.10–14

  • Nōn potes omnibus satis facere.

    You can’t satisfy everyone.Traupman 107

  • ex tuā sententiā

    to your satisfactionTraupman 374

See also satisfy, enjoy, enough.
